findings.title: Indemnification
findings.deviation: Business Associate shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Covered Entity, its Affiliates and their respective trustees, officers, employees and agents from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) any Privacy Event involving Business Associate or any Subcontractor; (b) any breach of this BAA by Business Associate or any Subcontractor; or (c) any violation of HIPAA or Texas Privacy Law by Business Associate or any Subcontractor, including without limitation regulatory fines, civil monetary penalties, costs of notification of Individuals, regulators and media, call-center support, credit monitoring and identity theft protection for affected Individuals, forensic investigation, and reasonable attorneys' fees.
findings.impact: AtliQ must accept this clause as it is more comprehensive than the playbook's mutual cap and carve-outs. However, AtliQ should ensure that the carve-outs are clear and that the scope of the indemnity is reasonable.
findings.quote: Business Associate shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Covered Entity, its Affiliates and their respective trustees, officers, employees and agents from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) any Privacy Event involving Business Associate or any Subcontractor; (b) any breach of this BAA by Business Associate or any Subcontractor; or (c) any violation of HIPAA or Texas Privacy Law by Business Associate or any Subcontractor, including without limitation regulatory fines, civil monetary penalties, costs of notification of Individuals, regulators and media, call-center support, credit monitoring and identity theft protection for affected Individuals, forensic investigation, and reasonable attorneys' fees.
findings.counterPosition: Each party indemnifies the other for third-party claims caused by its own breach or negligence; no indemnity for losses caused by the indemnified party's own negligence; indemnities subject to the liability cap (IP infringement excepted).

findings.title: Insurance
findings.deviation: Business Associate shall maintain, throughout the term of this BAA and for three (3) years thereafter, cyber liability and network security and privacy insurance with limits of not less than Five Million U.S. Dollars ($5,000,000) per claim and in the aggregate, covering notification costs, regulatory defense and penalties, and third-party claims arising from Privacy Events, and shall name Covered Entity as an additional insured.
findings.impact: AtliQ must accept this clause as it is more comprehensive than the playbook's requirement. However, AtliQ should ensure that the limits are appropriate and that the insurance coverage is adequate.
findings.quote: Business Associate shall maintain, throughout the term of this BAA and for three (3) years thereafter, cyber liability and network security and privacy insurance with limits of not less than Five Million U.S. Dollars ($5,000,000) per claim and in the aggregate, covering notification costs, regulatory defense and penalties, and third-party claims arising from Privacy Events, and shall name Covered Entity as an additional insured.
findings.counterPosition: Align required limits with current cover, or agree a timeline and cost to increase cover before signature.

fine.note: The BAA includes detailed data protection provisions, including notification requirements, cooperation with audits, and compliance with HIPAA and Texas Privacy Law. These provisions are in line with the playbook's expectations and do not require further negotiation.

The BAA includes a term that covers the return or destruction of PHI upon termination or expiration of the agreement, which is in line with the playbook's expectations and does not require further negotiation.
